case.title: Charles Nwaluno v. Independent National Electoral Commission

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Claimant filed suit on 20th May 2014 challenging termination of employment.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Defendant filed a notice of preliminary objection dated 5th November 2014, praying that the suit is statute barred.
interlocutory_applications: Notice of preliminary objection dated 5th November 2014 filed by the defendant.
procedural_events: Defendant filed notice of preliminary objection on 5th November 2014.
Claimant filed a 16-paragraph counter-affidavit and written address in opposition.
Defendant filed reply on points of law.

material_facts: Claimant was employed by the defendant.
Claimant's employment was terminated on 27th August 2009.
Claimant received letter of termination on 31st August 2009.

chronology.event: Claimant filed suit at National Industrial Court.
Defendant filed notice of preliminary objection.
Judgment delivered dismissing suit as statute barred.

admitted_facts: Cause of action arose on 31st August 2009.
Claimant's employment was terminated in August 2009.
disputed_facts: Whether defendant acted in bad faith or outside colour of its authority.
background_facts: Claimant was a staff of the defendant until termination.
facts.employment_relationship: Claimant was an employee of the defendant until termination on 27th August 2009.
facts.contractual_relationship: Employment relationship between claimant and defendant.
documentary_evidence: Letter of termination received by claimant on 31st August 2009.

issues_for_determination.issue: Whether or not the suit is statute barred having been commenced outside the statutory period of three (3) months from the accrual of the cause of action.

questions_of_law: Whether the suit is statute barred under section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Act.

claimant_arguments: Suit is not statute barred because defendant acted in bad faith, in abuse of office, and without semblance of legal justification.
Exceptions to statute of limitation based on continuing damage apply.
defendant_arguments: Suit is statute barred as it was filed outside the three months period after the cause of action arose on 27th August 2009.
Claimant received termination letter on 31st August 2009 and filed suit on 20th May 2014, well outside the three-month period.
No evidence of bad faith or abuse of office by defendant.
submissions: Defendant submitted that the suit is statute barred under section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Act.
Claimant submitted that the suit is not statute barred due to bad faith and abuse of office by defendant.

party_authorities.proposition: Support for exception to statute of limitation.

party_authorities.proposition: Support for exception to statute of limitation.

party_authorities.proposition: Support for exception to statute of limitation.

evidential_findings.evidence: Claimant's counter-affidavit and statement of claim.
evidential_findings.finding: No evidence of bad faith or abuse of office by defendant.

findings_of_fact.finding: Cause of action arose on 31st August 2009 when claimant received termination letter.

findings_of_fact.issue: Bad faith or abuse of office
findings_of_fact.finding: No evidence that defendant acted in bad faith or outside colour of its authority.

findings_of_law.finding: Suit is statute barred under section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Act as it was filed more than three months after accrual of cause of action.
Exception based on continuing damage does not apply as termination is a completed act, not continuing.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The cause of action arose on 31st August 2009. The suit was filed on 20th May 2014, outside the three-month period stipulated by section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Act. The claimant failed to show that the defendant acted in bad faith or outside the colour of its authority. The exception for continuing damage does not apply because the termination was a completed act. Therefore, the suit is statute barred.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether or not the suit is statute barred having been commenced outside the statutory period of three (3) months from the accrual of the cause of action.

arguments.claimant: Suit is not statute barred because defendant acted in bad faith, in abuse of office, and without semblance of legal justification; exceptions based on continuing damage apply.
arguments.defendant: Suit is statute barred as it was filed outside the three months period after the cause of action arose on 27th August 2009; no evidence of bad faith.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The parties agree that the cause of action arose on 31st August 2009. The claimant's counter-affidavit and claim do not show bad faith or abuse of office. The exception for continuing damage does not apply because termination is a completed act. The suit was filed on 20th May 2014, outside the three-month period.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: An action against a public officer must be commenced within three months of the accrual of the cause of action unless the defendant acted in bad faith or outside the colour of its authority; termination of employment is a completed act, not a continuing damage.

holdings.issue: Whether or not the suit is statute barred

ratio_decidendi.principle: Actions against public officers must be filed within three months of accrual of cause of action unless bad faith or abuse of office is shown.
ratio_decidendi.application: Claimant filed suit more than three months after termination and failed to show bad faith.

statutory_interpretation.application: Claimant's suit filed outside three months, thus statute barred.
